topIssues.title: Inbox and X verify lose inbound X DMs behind the owner's replies
topIssues.author: hermesagent270-commits
topIssues.body:
The LifeOps X DM cache holds outbound DMs alongside inbound ones. `readXInboundDms` and the inbox X DM fetch read the newest N rows and only then drop the outbound ones. As a result, the owner's recent replies hide inbound DMs from the inbox, and X verify under-reports inbound DMs.

**Acceptance:**
- The direction is filtered before `LIMIT`.
- Tests cover a real-PGlite repository read and the inbox fetch.

topIssues.title: listInbox answers "No unread messages" from an all-read cache without a live pull
topIssues.author: lumix5
topIssues.body:
### Problem

On develop `229502c357`, `plugins/plugin-assistant/src/features/messaging/triage/actions/listInbox.ts` serves the cached TriageService store whenever it is non-empty and only triggers a live `triage()` pull when the cache is completely empty. `MessageRefStore` keeps every ref a sweep ever handed it and never prunes read rows, so once the cached view contains only read messages, the action permanently answers "No unread messages across connected platforms." for the rest of the process lifetime while the authoritative connectors hold new unread mail.

### Reproduction and expected behavior

1. A `triage` sweep stores refs that are all `isRead` (or every ref in the store becomes read).
2. New unread mail arrives on the connector.
3. MESSAGE `list_inbox` ("show me unread across all platforms") → the cached path runs `rankScored`, filters unread to zero, and reports "No unread messages across connected platforms." without consulting any adapter.

Expected: a cached view with zero unread must fall through to the same live pull an empty cache gets, so the empty answer is only reported after the authoritative sources agree. An empty result after that live pull stays truthful.

### Acceptance

- An all-read cache triggers exactly one live pull; the returned unread view comes from the live result.
- When the live pull also yields no unread, the explicit empty-inbox result is reported (now live-verified, and the adapter pull is observable).
- Existing cached-unread and empty-cache behaviors are unchanged.
- Tests cover both cases against the real action handler.

topIssues.title: Follow-up: CVE IDs for the two fixed desktop security issues (#33034, #33036)
topIssues.author: CopperKoi
topIssues.body:
Hi @lalalune @lumix5,

First off, genuine respect for this project — an open-source agentic OS with this
breadth (multi-platform desktop app, plugin runtime, agent API) is rare, and the
engineering quality shows. Case in point: my security report got a fix PR within
about an hour, and both issues were verified with regression tests and closed
within two days. That turnaround is among the best I've seen in open source.

I'm the reporter of #33034 and #33036. Since both are already fixed on develop
(#33040, #33142, #33169), I'm opening this only as a follow-up to a request I
left on both threads on Oct 4, which I suspect went unnoticed — quite
understandable, since both were closed by then.

## The request

Could you help get CVE IDs assigned for these two vulnerabilities?

For context on why it matters: users running `@elizaos/app` ≤ 2.0.3-beta.7 are
exposed to silent theft of the OWNER-level token / plaintext stored provider
keys by any website they visit. A published GHSA + CVE is how most users and
scanners learn that a desktop update is security-critical, and it also records
how quickly you fixed it.

Thanks again for the fast fixes!

topIssues.title: Goal check-in responses revert concurrent goal edits
topIssues.author: hermesagent270-commits
topIssues.body:
Recording a goal check-in response writes the whole goal back from a read taken before the check-in task completes. A rename, status change, or review written in the meantime is reverted.

**Acceptance:**
- Check-ins persist only their own fields.
- A real-runtime test covers a concurrent edit.

topIssues.title: Goal review reverts concurrent goal edits and check-ins
topIssues.author: hermesagent270-commits
topIssues.body:
A goal review writes the whole goal row back from a snapshot taken before an LLM evaluation, or before a loop over every goal. Edits and check-ins written to the goal in the meantime are reverted: the title or status changes back, and new check-in log entries disappear.

**Acceptance:**
- Reviews persist only their own fields.
- A real-database test covers a concurrent edit.

topPRs.title: feat(app): serve authenticated self-hosted Cartesia voice sessions
topPRs.author: NubsCarson
topPRs.body:
Self-hosted clients requested realtime voice endpoints that the app host did not serve. Add owner-session-authenticated health, consent, mint, revoke and WebSocket routes using the existing Cartesia Ink/Sonic pipeline and canonical conversation stream. Preserve conversation/runtime binding, CSRF, pairing revocation and cancellation; provider credentials remain server-side. The reusable pipeline has explicit publishable host exports and Cloud compatibility entrypoints.

Normalize WebSocket messages using the transport's `isBinary` flag. Bun exposes text through its DOM-style listener as a Buffer; text hello/control frames now remain text, while binary audio cannot authenticate as JSON. Apply the same normalization to incoming sessions and outgoing Ink/Sonic sockets.

Validation on Node 24.15.0 and Bun 1.4.2:

- 13 authenticated HTTP/WebSocket/SQLite tests passed, covering ownership, CSRF, scope, replay, expiry, revocation, runtime reset and stopping after provider configuration becomes unavailable.
- 6 Node transport tests passed, including a subprocess run of the 5 Bun transport tests; direct Bun run also passed 5/5. These exercise real local TCP sockets and the actual Ink/Sonic adapters.
- 4 existing VoiceSession usage tests passed. App/host typechecks, host build, targeted lint, publish graph and default-condition imports passed; a focused Worker-condition voice bundle resolved successfully.

Live validation on the combined integration: a prerecorded spoken question completed real Cartesia STT, one runtime-selected model call, and Cartesia TTS. The current-clock correction in the integration produced the correct owner-local date. Returned PCM contained four seconds of audio; first returned audio arrived 3.62 seconds after final transcription. This is host transport acceptance; a subsequent physical Android turn on combined source 22ca6da3c253 also passed microphone capture, a Mac-hosted model reply, audible phone playback confirmed by the tester, and visible voice animation. The session was closed back to text afterward. Physical acoustic latency was not measured. Earlier handshake and socket failures are retained. Combined repository verification passed on integration a69027ea0d1; publication changes match the reviewed source files.

Additional authentication check: disposable real SQLite browser/machine sessions passed the actual host bridge and conversation-list handler with trusted-loopback bypass disabled. Browser cookie and browser session-ID bearer access, plus cookie voice health/consent/mint, succeeded; anonymous and revoked sessions returned401. The relevant authentication path is unchanged from the originally reviewed head. This addresses the concern about forwarding the browser session ID as bearer authority. No provider call was made by this check.

Review cleanup: removed redundant undefined-field filtering before JSON serialization and simplified the phrase empty-result branch while preserving the public flush boundary. Six focused rendering/override tests passed; the existing physical voice acceptance above remains the device evidence. No new audio test was run.

Final combined repository verification passed (exit 0) on clean integration `243ee6c6f5a61953713bede3da23daa1c1c275e8`. Every file added by this review update matches that verified source exactly; the isolated update has no conflicts with checked develop `65621da3a424f8fcdce760db5c9c414117082e18`.

topPRs.title: feat(app): connect reviewed Android Clock handoffs
topPRs.author: NubsCarson
topPRs.body:
# Relates to

Existing approved phone [#30844](https://github.com/elizaOS/eliza/issues/30844) and [#31025](https://github.com/elizaOS/eliza/issues/31025).

# Change

Clock requests use the existing proposal, approval, claim and receipt flow. Owners review the exact request before separate native consent. Unknown results are reconciled without replay. Recurrence requires the negotiated v2 capability. A Clock-only executor exposes only operations it supports, while separately authorized app actions remain available.

The native instruction now defines the existing set, show, dismiss and snooze meanings under those capability checks. Show opens Android Clock without creating or changing an alarm. It is not generic app navigation, and it still requires native approval. Set may create or update an alarm; dismiss and snooze may change one. An opened receipt proves handoff, not final alarm state or ringing.

Exact action selection uses the existing DISCOVER_ACTIONS names interface. It does not request the nonexistent candidateActionNames discovery parameter or add an unconditional discovery stage.

# Why this implementation

The fix uses the existing capability, permission, consent, proposal and receipt gates. It adds guidance for current effects, not a new native effect. Native Java/Kotlin, manifest, dependencies and private custody remain unchanged. The source overlay retains MAIN/LAUNCHER; alarm/timer intent ownership and default Clock-role activation remain intentionally absent.

# Scope and testing

This update changes only context-assembly.ts and the existing real device-actions test from reviewed0d1189a99d6fe4ae20796b1ca6c60d0948549e20. The69 other PR files retain their bytes. The settled Clock UI and its owning test remain exact8020, already published atb176. The71-file scope is unchanged.

Owning qualification for this operation mapping passed77 tests, typecheck and lint. Earlier discovery qualification and native artifact proofs remain separate evidence. The27bf APK has an honest renderer, the same signer and16KiB alignment;181 classes,108 generated sources and690 non-renderer payloads remained exact.

A safe future Google Clock alarm was created through explicit native consent, read back and removed. The original two disabled alarms remained unchanged; native journal reached COMPLETE/OPENED. No ringing was tested. The separate foreground-return correction preserves settled results through refresh. The current live SHOW semantic retest is still active and is not yet accepted.

## How to test

1. Use the compatible enrolled Android app with the original owner and negotiated Clock capabilities.
2. Request SHOW through the Clock handoff operation. Review and approve it; confirm that it opens system Clock without creating or changing an alarm.
3. Test supported set/dismiss/snooze requests only with explicit device authority. Preserve exact repeat days; v1 must reject recurrence.
4. Return from external Clock. Check that a settled receipt remains visible through refresh and uncertain outcomes do not replay effects.
5. Verify an owned future canary and remove only that canary. Dispatch alone is insufficient proof of alarm state or ringing.

## Qualification and current limits

Canonical `bun run verify` passed298/298 on combined source `f59cbaff666b90d6a39938eadb3c83a13dcb84c6`, tree `0800a2ff4ab9f9a1ce2a843df29476acbfea8bfb`. Owning extractor coverage passed99 cases and Clock context coverage passed77. Independent review found no blocker. These are combined-source results, not fresh canonical runs on the split PR branches.

The combined backend was adopted with owner, history and domain preservation controls passing. Renderer27bf remains compatible because these seven changes are backend and tests only. Fresh live projection/certificate and Clock SHOW retests are active; their final acceptance is pending. Keep this PR in draft. No merge, promotion or deployment is included.

# Evidence Gate

<!-- evidence-head:0d4e1b574d965c384804a0442872b599e8ae6fa0 -->
<!-- evidence-row:before-screenshots -->
- [ ] Before desktop/mobile images: required public attachments missing.
<!-- evidence-row:after-screenshots -->
- [ ] After desktop/mobile images: required public attachments missing.
<!-- evidence-row:walkthrough-video -->
- [ ] Uploaded MP4 explainer/walkthrough: missing; screenshots do not replace video.
<!-- evidence-row:backend-logs -->

<!-- evidence-row:frontend-logs -->

<!-- evidence-row:llm-trajectory -->

<!-- evidence-row:domain-artifacts -->

<!-- evidence-row:ocr-review -->

## Known gaps

Public attachments above remain incomplete. Current live semantic retests are pending. Historical failures and source-specific results are retained. This draft does not claim universal latency, minimal input or production readiness. Existing pinned dependencies were reused; no new install or APK build was performed for these backend corrections.

## Deployment
